summary: Submitted a new Candidate (action=continue) on the A3 recovery responsibility that the map had only as a deferred surface. Principal Fact F-log-persisted, lifecycle preservation, direct behavior B-follower-append (the consumer that classifies incoming entries against the cached identity), with B-snapshot-install as cause/context, activity context A1/A3, and a new SourceRange S-logstore-monotonic (log.go:137-146) for the MonotonicLogStore contract. Sourced lead: installSnapshot installs the snapshot, sets lastApplied/lastSnapshot and then, for a monotonic LogStore, calls removeOldLogs which deletes every log entry, but it never calls setLastLog - whereas the sibling leader-side restoreUserSnapshot does call setLastLog for the same reason. For a monotonic store the log store can thus be emptied while raftState.lastLogIndex/lastLogTerm still name entries the store no longer holds, so getLastEntry/AppendEntriesResponse.LastLog and the appendEntries classification loop (r.getLastLog()) can report and compare a non-existent last entry, making the follower reject the leader's subsequent AppendEntries and potentially loop on snapshots instead of catching up. This is the same divergence class as the first confirmed finding but reached through a legal InstallSnapshot history with no store failure, and it also corrects the earlier assumption that the snapshot path re-derives the reported identity. Counterevidence records that non-monotonic stores retain trailing entries via compactLogs, that an at-or-below-snapshot cache is rescued by the max() in getLastEntry/getLastIndex, and that the leader's post-install nextIndex plus any successful StoreLogs would call setLastLog; the unknowns fix the next discriminator (whether the cache can legally exceed the snapshot index, whether the rejection loop terminates, and how common monotonic stores are). No defect is presumed. The two earlier findings both remain confirmed (30950ca0199d4260b28f48b85bb6c269, 3ab05037...), and preflight returned valid:true.
